newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian forward dlr premiums up on corporate demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian forward dlr premiums up on corporate demand.

text.p: The rupee weakened in the forward market in late afternoon trade Monday after a leading petrochemicals firm bought dollars for one-year delivery, dealers said.
"They are buying spot one year forward - for August 20, 1998," said a dealer at a major bank.

Demand from the firm hit the market at a time when premiums are already on the rise due to a spurt in call money rates and speculation that a correction of the overvalued rupee is likely, dealers said.
Premiums on July-delivery dollars jumped to 1.90/1.93 rupees from 1.73/1.76 opening, dealers said. Premiums rose across the board -- as much as 0.16/0.17 rupee in some maturities, they said.
"It is corporate demand, not speculation," said a dealer.
There was corporate covering especially in September to July maturities, dealers said.
in the spot market, the rupee gained against the U.S. currency and was quoted at 35.705/712 per dollar in latest deals from 35.72/73 opening.
